# Settlers of Catan iOS v1 Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Build a native iOS Settlers of Catan app (Swift/SwiftUI) playable single-player, 1 human vs 3 heuristic AI bots, base-game rules, with a colonist.io-style flat visual theme and local auto-save.

**Architecture:** Three-layer Swift Package structure inside one Xcode project generated by XcodeGen: `CatanEngine` (pure rules/state, zero UI deps), `CatanAI` (heuristic bots built only on `CatanEngine`'s public API), `Settlers` (SwiftUI app target consuming both). Bots and humans submit moves through the identical `RulesEngine.apply(_:to:)` entrypoint.

**Tech Stack:** Swift 6.3, SwiftUI, Swift Testing (`import Testing`), XcodeGen (project.yml → .xcodeproj), Swift Package Manager (local packages under `Packages/`), iOS 17+ deployment target, iOS Simulator only.

## Global Constraints

- Deployment target: iOS 17.0. Swift tools version: 6.0 (packages), Swift 6 language mode for app target.
- No third-party dependencies beyond XcodeGen (a build tool, not a runtime dependency) — engine/AI/app use only Foundation/SwiftUI/Swift Testing.
- `GameState` and all its nested types must be `Codable` and `Sendable`.
- Bots must only act through `RulesEngine`'s public legal-move API — no privileged internal access.
- Base game only: 4 players (1 human at index 0, 3 bots at 1-3), 19 tiles, standard port layout, no expansions.
- Commit after every task; push to `origin/main` after every commit (per user's standing instruction).
- Visual style: flat-shaded hexes, crisp vector resource icons, bright saturated per-resource colors, minimal chrome (colonist.io-like) — applies to all Task 13+ view work.
- Every engine/AI task must leave `swift test` green in its package before commit; every app task must leave the app building (`xcodebuild build`) before commit.

## Board Geometry Reference (used by Tasks 2 and 13)

Tiles use axial coordinates `(q, r)`. The standard Catan board is the 19 hexes within radius 2 of `(0,0)`: all `(q,r)` with `q,r,-q-r` each in `-2...2`.

Each tile has 6 corners and 6 edges. A **vertex** is uniquely identified by the canonical, sorted set of the 1-3 tile coordinates that touch it. To compute this: for a given tile `(q,r)` and corner direction `0...5`, the corner touches that tile and its two neighbor tiles that also share that corner (some may be off-board, which is fine — off-board coordinates still canonicalize consistently, they're just never used as a "the tile is on the board" check). Concretely:

```swift
// The 6 axial neighbor directions, index-matched to corner geometry.
let neighborDirections: [(Int, Int)] = [(1,0), (1,-1), (0,-1), (-1,0), (-1,1), (0,1)]

// Corner `i` of tile (q,r) is shared by tile (q,r), neighbor(i), and neighbor(i+1 mod 6).
func cornerTiles(of tile: HexCoordinate, corner i: Int) -> Set<HexCoordinate> {
    let n1 = neighborDirections[i]
    let n2 = neighborDirections[(i + 1) % 6]
    return [tile,
            HexCoordinate(q: tile.q + n1.0, r: tile.r + n1.1),
            HexCoordinate(q: tile.q + n2.0, r: tile.r + n2.1)]
}
```

`VertexID` wraps the sorted array of that set (sort by `(q, r)`) so the same physical corner produces the same ID regardless of which adjacent tile it's computed from. An **edge** is uniquely identified by the unordered pair of the two `VertexID`s at its ends (an edge is the segment between corner `i` and corner `i+1` of a tile). `EdgeID` wraps the sorted pair.

This lets Task 2 build the full board graph by iterating all 19 on-board tiles × 6 corners, canonicalizing, and deduplicating into the vertex/edge sets — no separate off-board vertex filtering is needed for graph construction, but the board should also expose `Board.onBoardVertices` / `onBoardEdges` (only vertices/edges touching ≥1 on-board tile) since those are the only ones playable.

**Files:**

- Create: `Packages/CatanEngine/Sources/CatanEngine/BoardGeneration.swift`
- Test: `Packages/CatanEngine/Tests/CatanEngineTests/BoardGenerationTests.swift`

**Interfaces:**
- Produces:
  - `public enum Resource: String, Codable, CaseIterable, Sendable { case brick, lumber, ore, grain, wool }`
  - `public enum DevCardType: String, Codable, CaseIterable, Sendable { case knight, roadBuilding, yearOfPlenty, monopoly, victoryPoint }`
  - `public struct HexCoordinate: Hashable, Codable, Sendable { public let q: Int; public let r: Int }`
  - `public struct VertexID: Hashable, Codable, Sendable, Comparable { /* wraps sorted [HexCoordinate] */ }`
  - `public struct EdgeID: Hashable, Codable, Sendable { /* wraps sorted pair of VertexID */; public let a: VertexID; public let b: VertexID }`
  - `public enum TileKind: String, Codable, Sendable { case resource(Resource), desert }` — implemented as `public enum TileKind: Codable, Sendable, Equatable { case resource(Resource); case desert }` (no raw value, since it carries an associated value)
  - `public struct Tile: Codable, Sendable { public let coordinate: HexCoordinate; public let kind: TileKind; public let numberToken: Int? }` (`numberToken` nil for desert)
  - `public enum PortKind: Codable, Sendable, Equatable { case generic; case resource(Resource) }` (generic = 3:1, resource = 2:1 for that resource)
  - `public struct Port: Codable, Sendable { public let vertices: (VertexID, VertexID)... }` — represented as `public struct Port: Codable, Sendable { public let vertexA: VertexID; public let vertexB: VertexID; public let kind: PortKind }`
  - `public struct Board: Codable, Sendable { public let tiles: [Tile]; public let ports: [Port]; public let onBoardVertices: Set<VertexID>; public let onBoardEdges: Set<EdgeID>; public var robberTile: HexCoordinate }`
    - `public func neighborTiles(of vertex: VertexID) -> [HexCoordinate]`
    - `public func adjacentVertices(of vertex: VertexID) -> [VertexID]`
    - `public func edgesTouching(_ vertex: VertexID) -> [EdgeID]`
    - `public func vertices(of edge: EdgeID) -> (VertexID, VertexID)`
  - `public enum BoardGenerator { public static func standard() -> Board; public static func randomized(seed: UInt64) -> Board }`
    - `standard()` uses the fixed classic tile/number layout (see Step 4).
    - `randomized(seed:)` shuffles the 18 resource tiles + desert and the 18 number tokens using a seeded `RandomNumberGenerator`, re-rolling (retrying the shuffle) if any 6 or 8 token ends up adjacent to another 6 or 8 — this is the "balanced" constraint. Ports stay in their fixed standard positions (only tile/number placement is randomized) to keep vertex/port math simple and matching real Catan practice.

```swift
// HexCoordinate.swift
public struct HexCoordinate: Hashable, Codable, Sendable, Comparable {
    public let q: Int
    public let r: Int

    public init(q: Int, r: Int) { self.q = q; self.r = r }

    public static func < (lhs: HexCoordinate, rhs: HexCoordinate) -> Bool {
        (lhs.q, lhs.r) < (rhs.q, rhs.r)
    }

    public static let neighborDirections: [(Int, Int)] =
        [(1, 0), (1, -1), (0, -1), (-1, 0), (-1, 1), (0, 1)]

    public func neighbor(_ direction: Int) -> HexCoordinate {
        let d = HexCoordinate.neighborDirections[((direction % 6) + 6) % 6]
        return HexCoordinate(q: q + d.0, r: r + d.1)
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Write `VertexID.swift` and `EdgeID.swift`**

```swift
// VertexID.swift
public struct VertexID: Hashable, Codable, Sendable, Comparable {
    /// The 1-3 tile coordinates that meet at this corner, always stored sorted.
    public let touchingTiles: [HexCoordinate]

    public init(touchingTiles: Set<HexCoordinate>) {
        self.touchingTiles = touchingTiles.sorted()
    }

    public static func < (lhs: VertexID, rhs: VertexID) -> Bool {
        lhs.touchingTiles.lexicographicallyPrecedes(rhs.touchingTiles) { a, b in a < b }
    }
}
```
```swift
// EdgeID.swift
public struct EdgeID: Hashable, Codable, Sendable {
    public let a: VertexID
    public let b: VertexID

    public init(_ v1: VertexID, _ v2: VertexID) {
        if v1 < v2 { a = v1; b = v2 } else { a = v2; b = v1 }
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Write `BoardGeneration.swift` with the standard fixed layout**

Standard resource counts: 4 grain, 4 wool, 4 lumber, 3 brick, 3 ore, 1 desert (19 tiles). Standard number tokens (18, desert has none): `5, 2, 6, 3, 8, 10, 9, 12, 11, 4, 8, 10, 9, 4, 5, 6, 3, 11`. Use the well-known standard layout ordering (spiral placement starting from one corner going clockwise, matching the physical Catan board) — implement by defining the 19 board coordinates in spiral order (center outward) and zipping fixed resource/number arrays chosen so no 6/8 is adjacent (this is the documented standard board). Ports: 4 generic (3:1) + 1 each of the 5 resources (2:1) = 9 ports total, placed at the standard fixed edge positions around the board perimeter.

import Testing
@testable import CatanEngine

@Test func standardBoardHas19TilesAndOneDesert() {
    let board = BoardGenerator.standard()
    #expect(board.tiles.count == 19)
    #expect(board.tiles.filter { $0.kind == .desert }.count == 1)
}

@Test func standardBoardHasNoAdjacentSixOrEight() {
    let board = BoardGenerator.standard()
    let hot = board.tiles.filter { $0.numberToken == 6 || $0.numberToken == 8 }
    for tile in hot {
        for dir in 0..<6 {
            let n = tile.coordinate.neighbor(dir)
            if let neighborTile = board.tiles.first(where: { $0.coordinate == n }) {
                #expect(!(neighborTile.numberToken == 6 || neighborTile.numberToken == 8))
            }
        }
    }
}

@Test func randomizedBoardIsDeterministicForSameSeed() {
    let b1 = BoardGenerator.randomized(seed: 42)
    let b2 = BoardGenerator.randomized(seed: 42)
    #expect(b1.tiles.map(\.coordinate) == b2.tiles.map(\.coordinate))
    #expect(b1.tiles.map(\.numberToken) == b2.tiles.map(\.numberToken))
}

@Test func boardHas9Ports() {
    #expect(BoardGenerator.standard().ports.count == 9)
}

@Test func vertexCanonicalizationIsConsistentAcrossSharedTiles() {
    let board = BoardGenerator.standard()
    // Every on-board edge's two vertices must each be in onBoardVertices.
    for edge in board.onBoardEdges {
        #expect(board.onBoardVertices.contains(edge.a))
        #expect(board.onBoardVertices.contains(edge.b))
    }
}

  - `public struct GameState: Codable, Sendable { public var board: Board; public var players: [Player]; public var phase: GamePhase; public var bank: [Resource: Int]; public var devCardDeck: [DevCardType]; public var lastDiceRoll: Int?; public var longestRoadPlayer: PlayerID?; public var largestArmyPlayer: PlayerID?; public var pendingTradeOffers: [TradeOffer]; public var log: [String] }`
  - `public enum MoveError: Error, Sendable, Equatable { case notYourTurn, illegalPlacement, insufficientResources, wrongPhase, invalidTradeTarget, other(String) }`
  - `public enum RulesEngine { public static func legalMoves(for state: GameState) -> [GameMove]; public static func apply(_ move: GameMove, by player: PlayerID, to state: inout GameState) throws }`
  - `public enum GameSetup { public static func newGame(board: Board) -> GameState }` — creates 4 players (human index 0), full bank (19 each of brick/lumber/wool/grain/ore... actually standard bank: 19 each resource), 25 dev cards (14 knight, 5 VP, 2 each of road building/year of plenty/monopoly), phase `.setupForward(playerIndex: 0)`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Write `GameState.swift`** with the `GameState` struct and `GameSetup.newGame(board:)`.

- [ ] **Step 4: Write `SetupPhase.swift`** implementing the setup-phase-specific legal move logic and application:
  - `setupForward`/`setupBackward` alternate through player indices 0→3 then 3→0 (snake order), each player placing one settlement then one adjacent road per turn.
  - Legal settlement vertices: on-board, unoccupied, and at least 2 edges away from every existing settlement/city (distance rule).
  - Legal initial road: must be one of the edges touching the settlement just placed in this same sub-turn.
  - On the second placement (backward pass) only, the player immediately receives resources from all tiles adjacent to that settlement (first settlement grants nothing, matching standard rules).
  - After the last backward placement (player index 0's second settlement), phase transitions to `.rollDice(playerIndex: 0)`.

- [ ] **Step 5: Write `RulesEngine.swift`** with `legalMoves(for:)` and `apply(_:by:to:)` dispatching to `SetupPhase` when `phase` is `.setupForward`/`.setupBackward`, and throwing `.wrongPhase` for any other move type during setup. (Later tasks extend the `switch` for other phases.)

- [ ] **Step 6: Write `SetupPhaseTests.swift`**

```swift
import Testing
@testable import CatanEngine

@Test func setupPhaseFollowsSnakeOrder() {
    var state = GameSetup.newGame(board: BoardGenerator.standard())
    let p0 = PlayerID(index: 0)
    let firstVertex = board(state).onBoardVertices.sorted().first!
    try! RulesEngine.apply(.placeInitialSettlement(firstVertex), by: p0, to: &state)
    let firstEdge = state.board.edgesTouching(firstVertex).first!
    try! RulesEngine.apply(.placeInitialRoad(firstEdge), by: p0, to: &state)
    if case .setupForward(let idx) = state.phase {
        #expect(idx == 1)
    } else {
        Issue.record("expected setupForward(1), got \(state.phase)")
    }
}

@Test func secondSettlementGrantsResources() {
    var state = GameSetup.newGame(board: BoardGenerator.standard())
    // Fast-forward through players 0-3 forward pass, then 3-0 backward pass,
    // placing legal moves each time via RulesEngine.legalMoves(for:).first!
    while case .setupForward = state.phase {
        let move = RulesEngine.legalMoves(for: state).first!
        let player = currentSetupPlayer(state.phase)
        try! RulesEngine.apply(move, by: player, to: &state)
    }
    let beforeTotal = totalResources(state.players[3])
    // player 3 goes first in backward pass; placing their settlement then road
    let settleMove = RulesEngine.legalMoves(for: state).first!
    try! RulesEngine.apply(settleMove, by: PlayerID(index: 3), to: &state)
    let afterTotal = totalResources(state.players[3])
    #expect(afterTotal >= beforeTotal) // grants resources unless placed on desert-only spot
}

private func board(_ state: GameState) -> Board { state.board }
private func totalResources(_ p: Player) -> Int { p.resources.values.reduce(0, +) }
private func currentSetupPlayer(_ phase: GamePhase) -> PlayerID {
    switch phase {
    case .setupForward(let i), .setupBackward(let i): return PlayerID(index: i)
    default: fatalError("not in setup")
    }
}
```

**Interfaces:**

- Produces:
  - `MainPhase.rollDice(state: inout GameState, roll: Int)` — applies production for a given roll (roll is injected so tests are deterministic; the real random roll is generated by `RulesEngine.apply(.rollDice, ...)` internally using `Int.random(in:1...6)` twice, but `MainPhase` exposes a roll-injectable function for testability).

  - `Building.canBuildSettlement(_ vertex: VertexID, for player: PlayerID, in state: GameState) -> Bool` (distance rule + must connect to player's own road network, except during setup).
  - `Building.canBuildCity(_ vertex: VertexID, for player: PlayerID, in state: GameState) -> Bool` (must be player's existing settlement).
  - `LongestRoad.compute(for state: GameState) -> PlayerID?` — longest continuous road ≥5 for each player (longest simple path in that player's road-edge graph, broken by opponent settlements/cities sitting on the path), returns the player with the strict longest (ties: current holder keeps the bonus per official rules; if no current holder and tie, return nil — no one gets it).

- [ ] **Step 1: Write `Building.swift`** with cost constants and the three `canBuild*` legality checks, using `Board.adjacentVertices`/`edgesTouching` from Task 2 and `Player.roads`/`settlements`/`cities` from Task 3.

- [ ] **Step 2: Write `LongestRoadTests.swift` first (TDD), covering: a simple 5-edge chain scoring 5, a branching network scoring only its longest simple path, and an opponent settlement in the middle of a road breaking it into two shorter segments.**

```swift
import Testing
@testable import CatanEngine

@Test func fiveConnectedRoadsGrantsLongestRoad() {
    var state = GameSetup.newGame(board: BoardGenerator.standard())
    let p0 = PlayerID(index: 0)
    let path = fiveEdgeChain(on: state.board) // helper: walk 5 connected on-board edges from a fixed start vertex
    for edge in path { state.players[0].roads.insert(edge) }
    #expect(LongestRoad.compute(for: state) == p0)
}

@Test func opponentSettlementBreaksRoadChain() {
    var state = GameSetup.newGame(board: BoardGenerator.standard())
    let path = fiveEdgeChain(on: state.board)
    for edge in path { state.players[0].roads.insert(edge) }
    let midVertex = state.board.vertices(of: path[2]).0
    state.players[1].settlements.insert(midVertex)
    #expect(LongestRoad.compute(for: state) != PlayerID(index: 0))
}

private func fiveEdgeChain(on board: Board) -> [EdgeID] {
    // Deterministic BFS from the lowest-sorted on-board vertex, walking 5 edges deep.
    var chain: [EdgeID] = []
    var current = board.onBoardVertices.sorted().first!
    var visited: Set<VertexID> = [current]
    while chain.count < 5 {
        let next = board.adjacentVertices(of: current).first { !visited.contains($0) }!
        chain.append(board.edgesTouching(current).first { board.vertices(of: $0).0 == next || board.vertices(of: $0).1 == next }!)
        visited.insert(next)
        current = next
    }
    return chain
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write `FullGameSimulationTests.swift`** — a critical end-to-end regression test that plays a complete game using only `RulesEngine.legalMoves`/`apply` with randomly-selected legal moves each turn (a "monkey test"), asserting the game reaches `.gameOver` within a bounded number of moves without ever throwing.

```swift
import Testing
@testable import CatanEngine

@Test func randomLegalPlayReachesGameOverWithoutErrors() {
    var state = GameSetup.newGame(board: BoardGenerator.randomized(seed: 7))
    var rng = SeededGenerator(seed: 7)
    var iterations = 0
    while true {
        if case .gameOver = state.phase { break }
        iterations += 1
        #expect(iterations < 20_000, "game did not terminate")
        if iterations >= 20_000 { break }
        let moves = RulesEngine.legalMoves(for: state)
        #expect(!moves.isEmpty, "no legal moves in phase \(state.phase)")
        guard let move = moves.randomElement(using: &rng) else { break }
        let player = activePlayer(state.phase)
        try! RulesEngine.apply(move, by: player, to: &state)
    }
}

private func activePlayer(_ phase: GamePhase) -> PlayerID {
    switch phase {
    case .setupForward(let i), .setupBackward(let i), .rollDice(let i), .mainTurn(let i), .movingRobber(let i):
        return PlayerID(index: i)
    case .discarding(let pending): return pending.first!
    case .gameOver: fatalError("game over")
    }
}

/// Deterministic RNG so this test is reproducible.
struct SeededGenerator: RandomNumberGenerator {
    var state: UInt64
    init(seed: UInt64) { state = seed &+ 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 }
    mutating func next() -> UInt64 {
        state ^= state << 13; state ^= state >> 7; state ^= state << 17
        return state
    }
}
```

### Task 10: AI Robber, Trade, and Dev Card Heuristics + Personalities

**Files:**
- Create: `Packages/CatanAI/Sources/CatanAI/RobberHeuristics.swift`
- Create: `Packages/CatanAI/Sources/CatanAI/TradeHeuristics.swift`

**Interfaces:**
- Produces:
  - `RobberHeuristics.chooseRobberTarget(state: GameState, player: PlayerID) -> (HexCoordinate, PlayerID?)` — maximizes disruption to the leading opponent (by VP) while excluding tiles touching the bot's own settlements when an alternative exists.
  - `TradeHeuristics.evaluate(offer: TradeOffer, receiver: PlayerID, state: GameState, personality: BotPersonality) -> Bool` — accepts if the `want` cards are less valuable to the receiver (by marginal-value-to-current-build-plan) than the `give` cards, scaled by `personality.tradeWillingness`.
  - `TradeHeuristics.proposeTrades(state: GameState, player: PlayerID, personality: BotPersonality) -> [TradeOffer]` — up to 1 proposal per turn when the bot is resource-blocked on its best build.
  - `DevCardHeuristics.shouldBuyDevCard(state: GameState, player: PlayerID) -> Bool` and `DevCardHeuristics.choosePlay(state: GameState, player: PlayerID) -> GameMove?` (e.g., play knight to unblock a good production tile or contest largest army; play year-of-plenty/monopoly when it completes an otherwise-unaffordable build).
  - `Bot.decide` extended: during `.mainTurn`, before/after `BuildPlanner`, also consider proposing/responding to trades and dev card plays via the above, using `personality` to weight the choice among all legal-move categories.

### Task 12: GameViewModel (Engine + AI + Persistence Integration)

**Files:**
- Create: `Settlers/ViewModels/GameViewModel.swift`
- Modify: `Settlers/ContentView.swift` (temporary: instantiate view model and print state, replaced properly in Task 15)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `GameState`, `GameSetup`, `RulesEngine`, `BoardGenerator` (`CatanEngine`); `Bot`, `BotPersonality` (`CatanAI`); `GameStore` (Task 11).
- Produces:
  - `@Observable public final class GameViewModel { public private(set) var state: GameState; public let humanPlayer = PlayerID(index: 0); public private(set) var isBotThinking: Bool; public init(); public func startNewGame(randomizedBoard: Bool); public func apply(_ move: GameMove) throws; public func runBotTurnIfNeeded() async }`
  - `apply(_:)` calls `RulesEngine.apply(move, by: humanPlayer, to: &state)` then `GameStore.shared.save(state)`, then triggers `runBotTurnIfNeeded()`.
  - `runBotTurnIfNeeded()`: while the active player (derived from `state.phase`) is not `humanPlayer` and `state.phase != .gameOver`, set `isBotThinking = true`, `try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(600))` (the "visible thinking" pacing from the design doc), compute the bot's move via the `Bot` matching that player's index (bots use `BotPersonality.balanced`/`.aggressive`/`.cautious` respectively for indices 1/2/3), apply it through the same `RulesEngine.apply`, save, loop; set `isBotThinking = false` when it's the human's turn again or the game ends.
  - `init()` calls `GameStore.shared.load()`; if non-nil, resumes that state; otherwise leaves `state` as a fresh `GameSetup.newGame(board: BoardGenerator.standard())` awaiting `startNewGame`.

### Task 13: Board Rendering (Canvas Hex Board + Pieces)

**Files:**
- Create: `Settlers/Theme/CatanTheme.swift`
- Create: `Settlers/Views/Board/HexGeometry.swift`
- Create: `Settlers/Views/Board/BoardView.swift`
- Create: `Settlers/Views/Board/TileView.swift` (as part of `BoardView`'s Canvas drawing, plus a lightweight overlay struct for tap targets)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `Board`, `Tile`, `TileKind`, `HexCoordinate`, `VertexID`, `EdgeID`, `Player` from `CatanEngine`; `GameViewModel` from Task 12.
- Produces:
  - `CatanTheme`: static `Color` constants per `Resource` (brick=terracotta orange, lumber=forest green, ore=slate gray, grain=gold/wheat yellow, wool=lime/light green, desert=sand beige) plus per-`PlayerID` colors (human=blue, bots=red/orange/white or similar 4 distinguishable colors) — flat, saturated, colonist.io-like.
  - `HexGeometry`: pure pixel-math struct `HexGeometry(origin: CGPoint, size: CGFloat)` with `func center(of tile: HexCoordinate) -> CGPoint`, `func corner(of tile: HexCoordinate, index: Int) -> CGPoint`, `func vertexPosition(_ vertex: VertexID, board: Board) -> CGPoint` (average of that vertex's touching-tile corner positions — robust since off-board tiles still produce a consistent geometric point), `func edgeMidpoint(_ edge: EdgeID, board: Board) -> CGPoint`.
  - `BoardView(state: GameState, onTapVertex: (VertexID) -> Void, onTapEdge: (EdgeID) -> Void, onTapTile: (HexCoordinate) -> Void)`: `Canvas` draws all hex tiles (fill by `TileKind`/`Resource` via `CatanTheme`), number tokens (text, red for 6/8), robber (dark circle on its tile), ports (small icon near the relevant edge); overlaid `ForEach` of invisible tappable circles at each on-board vertex (settlement/city tap targets, sized generously for touch) and invisible tappable capsules along each on-board edge (road tap targets); settlements/cities/roads themselves drawn as small `Shape`s (triangle-roof house for settlement, larger house for city, rounded rect for road) colored by owning player, using `.animation(.spring, value: state)`-driven position for a satisfying "place" animation.
